channel.title: AI Stupa Translation Project
channel.description: New English translations of texts from the Tibetan Buddhist canon, made by the AI Stupa (provisional, public domain).

item.title: The Tantra Called Glorious Vajra Mahākāla (Toh 416)
item.description: The Tantra Called Glorious Vajra Mahākāla, the Wrathful Protector, Source of Secret Accomplishment, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Vajra Mahākāla Krodhanātha Rahasya Siddhi Bhava Tantra and in Tibetan as Dpal rdo rje nag po chen po khros pa'i mgon po gsang ba dngos grub 'byung ba, is a tantric scripture centered on Mahākāla, the fierce protector deity of the Buddhist teachings. It opens with homage…

item.title: The Rite of the Fire Offering (Toh 1223)
item.description: The Rite of the Fire Offering, known in Sanskrit as the Homavidhi and in Tibetan as Jinsek gi Choga, is a short ritual manual in verse belonging to the cycle of the Hevajra Tantra, attributed in its colophon to the Indian master Saroruhavajra. Opening with homage to Hevajra and his consort Nairātmyā, it distinguishes an unsurpassed, an inner, and an outer fire offering, and then sets out the…

item.title: The Fivefold Pledge (Toh 1224)
item.description: The Fivefold Pledge, known in Sanskrit as the Samayapañca and in Tibetan as Damtsik Ngapa, is a short verse manual on the feast gathering (gaṇacakra), the communal tantric rite in which initiated practitioners assemble to make offerings, share consecrated food and drink, and sing and dance as deities. Opening with homage to Vajrasattva, it sets out when and where the feast should be held, the…

item.title: The Praise of the Bhaḍarāga of Glorious Hevajra (Toh 1225)
item.description: This text is the Praise of Glorious Hevajra in Twenty Verses, whose Sanskrit title is given as Śrī Hevajra Bhaḍarāga Stotra and whose Tibetan title is Dpal kye rdo rje'i bha ḍa rā ga'i bstod pa; it is attributed to the great accomplished master Saroruhavajra and was translated into Tibetan by the Indian preceptor Gayādhara and the Tibetan translator Shākya Yeshé. A devotional hymn in verse, it…

item.title: The Means of Accomplishment Called Glorious Ekavīra (Toh 1226)
item.description: The Means of Accomplishment Called Glorious Ekavīra, in Sanskrit Śrī Ekavīra Sādhana and in Tibetan Pal Pawo Chikpa zhe jawé Drubpé Tap, is a short tantric meditation manual, or sādhana, on Hevajra visualized as the "sole hero" without a surrounding retinue, joined with his consort Nairātmyā. Composed, according to its colophon, by the Indian master Vajraghaṇṭa and translated into Tibetan by the…

item.title: The Means of Accomplishing Glorious Hevajra (Toh 1227)
item.description: The Means of Accomplishing Glorious Hevajra, in Sanskrit Śrīhevajrasādhana and in Tibetan Pal Kyé Dorjé shejawé drubpé tap, is a concise sādhana, a practice manual for meditating on the tantric deity Hevajra, condensed from the Hevajra Tantra. It guides the practitioner from choosing a suitable place and making preliminary offerings, refuge and the four immeasurables, through meditation on…

item.title: The Rite of the Fire Offering from Glorious Hevajra (Toh 1228)
item.description: The Rite of the Fire Offering from Glorious Hevajra, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Hevajra Homavidhi and in Tibetan as Dpal kye rdo rje las sbyin sreg gi cho ga, is a concise ritual manual for performing the fire offering, or homa, within the practice of Hevajra, attributed in its colophon to the master Bodhigarbha and translated into Tibetan by the Indian preceptor Kamalaśrī with the monk Sherab…

item.title: The Ten Realities (Toh 1229)
item.description: This text is The Ten Realities, in Sanskrit Daśatattva and in Tibetan De kho na nyid bcu pa, a short ritual manual attributed to the Indian master Ḍombipa and translated into Tibetan by Dīpaṃkaraśrījñāna, also known as Atiśa, with the monk Gewé Lodrö. Drawing on the Hevajra Tantra, it sets out in brief the ten ritual topics a tantric master must know: the wheel of protection with its ten wrathful…

item.title: Advice on the Uncommon Meaning for Yogins and Yoginīs (Toh 1230)
item.description: Advice on the Uncommon Meaning for Yogins and Yoginīs, known in Tibetan as Rnal 'byor pha dang rnal 'byor ma rnams la thun mong ma yin pa'i don la gdams pa, and given in its Sanskrit title line in a garbled form that points to a "Yoga-yoginīnām asādhāraṇa-upadeśa," is a short tantric instruction attributed to the Indian master Ḍombi Heruka and compiled by the alms-going yogin Prajñāśrījñāna. It…

item.title: The Maṇḍala Rite Called The Emergence of Heruka (Toh 1270)
item.description: The Maṇḍala Rite Called The Emergence of Heruka, whose Sanskrit title appears to be Herukābhyudaya Maṇḍalavidhi and whose Tibetan title is He ru ka nye bar 'byung ba zhes bya ba'i dkyil 'khor gyi cho ga, is a concise ritual manual for constructing and working with the maṇḍala of the tantric deity Heruka. Opening with homage to Vajraḍāka and Hevajra and praising Heruka as the Innate One, the…

item.title: The Torma Rite of Glorious Hevajra (Toh 1287)
item.description: The Torma Rite of Glorious Hevajra, in Sanskrit Śrī Hevajra Balividhi and in Tibetan Pal Kyé Dorjé Tormé Chok, is a short tantric ritual manual on offering torma, ritual cakes, to the deities and spirits connected with the practice of Hevajra. Quoting scripture, the tantra and earlier masters on the great benefit of such offerings, it explains when torma should be given, to the twenty-four…

item.title: A Commentary on the Empowerment Section of the King of Tantras, the Glorious Kālacakra, called Unraveling the Vajra Words (Toh 1355)
item.description: Unraveling the Vajra Words, whose fuller title is A Commentary on the Empowerment Section of the King of Tantras, the Glorious Kālacakra, is known in Sanskrit as Śrī Kālacakratantrarājasya Sekaprakriyāvṛtti Vajrapadodghaṭī and in Tibetan as rgyud kyi rgyal po dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i dbang gi rab tu byed pa'i 'grel pa rdo rje'i tshig 'byed pa. It is a commentary on the section of the Kālacakra…

item.title: The Four-Limbed Sādhana of Glorious Kālacakra (Toh 1356)
item.description: The Four-Limbed Sādhana of Glorious Kālacakra, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Kālacakra Caturaṅga Sādhanopāyikā and in Tibetan as Dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i sgrub pa'i thabs yan lag bzhi pa, is a short verse manual of tantric practice centered on Kālacakra, the "Wheel of Time." It opens with homage to Mañjuśrī and Avalokiteśvara and hymns of praise to the deity, then sets out the meditation through…

item.title: The Sādhana of the Glorious Constellation Maṇḍala in Eleven Limbs (Toh 1357)
item.description: The Sādhana of the Glorious Constellation Maṇḍala in Eleven Limbs, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Nakṣatra Maṇḍala Sādhana Ekādaśāṅga and in Tibetan as Palden Gyukar gyi Kyilkhor gyi Druptap Yenlak Chuchikpa, is a ritual manual for meditating on the maṇḍala of the Kālacakra, or Wheel of Time, tantra, whose cosmic and astral symbolism gives the constellation maṇḍala its name. After paying homage to…

item.title: The Rite of the Maṇḍala of Glorious Kālacakra (Toh 1359)
item.description: The Rite of the Maṇḍala of Glorious Kālacakra, known in Sanskrit as Śrīkālacakramaṇḍalopāyikāvidhi and in Tibetan as Dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i dkyil 'khor gyi cho ga, is a ritual manual devoted to the maṇḍala of Kālacakra, the "Wheel of Time" deity of highest yoga tantra. It opens with homage to Kālacakra as the all-pervading lord whose nature unites method and wisdom and who destroys the terrors…

item.title: The Rite of the Maṇḍala of Glorious Kālacakra (Toh 1360)
item.description: The Rite of the Maṇḍala of Glorious Kālacakra, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Kālacakra Maṇḍalavidhi and in Tibetan as Pal Dükyi Khorlö Kyilkhor gyi Choga, is a ritual manual in verse for establishing and worshipping the maṇḍala of the Kālacakra, or Wheel of Time, tantra. Opening with homage to Kālacakra and to Avalokiteśvara, it sets out the maṇḍala rite in its two aspects of preparation and…

item.title: The Means of Accomplishing Glorious Connate Kālacakra (Toh 1361)
item.description: The Means of Accomplishing Glorious Connate Kālacakra, in Sanskrit the Śrī Kālacakra Sahaja Sādhana and in Tibetan Pal Dükyi Khorlo Lhenchik Kyepa Drubpé Tap, is a short Indian ritual and meditation manual for the practice of Kālacakra in his connate form, united with his consort. Written largely in verse, it moves from preparing the site, offering torma and expelling obstructors, through the…

item.title: The Coemergent Means of Accomplishment of Glorious Kālacakra (Toh 1362)
item.description: The Coemergent Means of Accomplishment of Glorious Kālacakra, Generated in an Instant, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Kālacakra Sahaja Sādhana and in Tibetan as Pal Dükyi Khorlo Kechik Gi Kyepé Lhenchik Kyepé Druptap, is a brief tantric meditation manual, or sādhana, for the practice of the deity Kālacakra. After paying homage to the body of great bliss and to the Ādibuddha, the first buddha, it…

item.title: The Six-Branched Yoga (Toh 1364)
item.description: The Six-Branched Yoga, known in Sanskrit as Ṣaḍaṅgayoga and in Tibetan as Sbyor ba yan lag drug pa, is a short tantric commentary attributed in its colophon to the bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets. It explains the six branches of yoga taught in the Later Tantra of Guhyasamāja, namely withdrawal, meditative concentration, breath control, retention, recollection, and absorption, showing…

item.title: The Sādhana Called the Ornament of the Essence of Glorious Kālacakra (Toh 1365)
item.description: The Sādhana Called the Ornament of the Essence of Glorious Kālacakra, in Sanskrit Śrī Kālacakragarbhālaṃkārasādhana and in Tibetan Dpal dus kyi 'khor lo'i snying po'i rgyan zhes bya ba'i sgrub thabs, is a tantric practice manual devoted to Kālacakra, the "Wheel of Time," attributed in its colophon to the great scholar, the brahmin Piṇḍo. It opens with homage to Vajradhara and to Kālacakra as the…

item.title: Pith Instructions on Kālacakra (Toh 1366)
item.description: The Pith Instructions on Kālacakra, known in Sanskrit as the Kālacakra Upadeśa and in Tibetan as Dü kyi Khorlö Men-ngak, is a brief tantric commentary attributed to the master Kālacakrapāda the Great and translated into Tibetan by the Indian preceptor Buddhākarabhadra with the translator Gyijo Dawé Özer. It sets out a series of verses on the completion-stage practice of the Kālacakra system and…

item.title: The Six-Branched Yoga (Toh 1367)
item.description: The Six-Branched Yoga, known in Sanskrit as the Ṣaḍaṅgayoga and in Tibetan as Jorwa Yenlak Drukpa, is a short Indian treatise on the completion-stage practice of the Kālacakra tradition, composed by the accomplished paṇḍita Anupamarakṣita and translated into Tibetan by the Indian scholar Vibhūticandra together with the translator of Nyal, Minyam Zangpo. Opening with homage to the great adept…

item.title: Commentary on the Six-Limbed Yoga (Toh 1368)
item.description: The Commentary on the Six-Limbed Yoga, known in Sanskrit as the Ṣaḍaṅgayogaṭīkā and in Tibetan as Sbyor ba yan lag drug pa'i 'grel pa, is a tantric commentary by the Indian paṇḍita Raviśrījñāna on the six-limbed yoga of the Kālacakra tradition, the system of withdrawal, meditative stabilization, breath control, retention, recollection and absorption that leads to the "empty forms" and to…

item.title: The Instruction of Glorious Kālacakra Called the Practice of Sun and Moon (Toh 1369)
item.description: The Instruction of Glorious Kālacakra Called the Practice of Sun and Moon, in Sanskrit the Śrī Kālacakra Upadeśa Sūryacandra Sādhana and in Tibetan Pal Dükyi Khorlö Damngak Nyima Dawa Druppa, is a Kālacakra completion-stage instruction set in a frame story. It tells how an Indian paṇḍita who had received the Kālacakra teachings at Mount Nemindhara was visited in the evening, at midnight, and at…

item.title: The Accomplishment of the Eye of Gnosis (Toh 1370)
item.description: The Accomplishment of the Eye of Gnosis, known in Sanskrit as the Jñānacakṣusādhana and in Tibetan as Yeshé Chen Drubpa, is a short verse instruction on the completion-stage practice of the Kālacakra tradition, attributed in its colophon to the master Kālapāda and translated into Tibetan by the Indian paṇḍita Vibhūticandra himself. Drawing on the Kālacakra tantra, it teaches how to cultivate the…

item.title: Illuminating the Essence of the Three Yogas (Toh 1371)
item.description: Illuminating the Essence of the Three Yogas, whose Sanskrit title appears in the Tibetan as Trijogi Hṛda Byākāśa, roughly Triyogahṛdayaprakāśa, and whose Tibetan title is Rnal 'byor gsum gyi snying po gsal ba, is a brief verse treatise on tantric meditation. It sets out the meditation of the Great Seal through three yogas, of blessing, of conceptual meditation, and of the natural state, and then…

item.title: Instruction on the Six-Branch Yoga (Toh 1372)
item.description: The Instruction on the Six-Branch Yoga, known in Tibetan as Jorwa Yenlak Drukgi Mengak and probably corresponding to a Sanskrit Ṣaḍaṅgayoga-upadeśa, is a short verse manual of completion-stage practice in the Kālacakra tradition. Opening with homage to the holy gurus and to Kālacakra, it sets out for initiated practitioners the six branches of withdrawal, meditative concentration, breath control…

item.title: An Instruction on the Six-Limbed Yoga (Toh 1374)
item.description: An Instruction on the Six-Limbed Yoga, known in Sanskrit as the Ṣaḍaṅgayoga Upadeśa and in Tibetan as Yenlak Druk gi Jorwé Mengak, is a brief verse manual of tantric meditation attributed to the Indian master Celupa and translated into Tibetan by the paṇḍita Mantraśrī and the translator Ra Chörab. Addressed to a practitioner who has received the four empowerments and seeks the state of great…

item.title: The Six-Limbed Yoga (Toh 1375)
item.description: The Six-Limbed Yoga, known in Sanskrit as the Yoga Ṣaḍaṅga and in Tibetan as the Rnal 'byor yan lag drug pa, is a brief verse instruction on the sixfold yoga of the completion stage of tantric practice. Opening with homage to Vajradhara, it names the six limbs of withdrawal, meditative concentration, breath control, retention, subsequent mindfulness and meditative absorption, and then describes…

item.title: The Garland of Yogas (Toh 1376)
item.description: The Garland of Yogas, known in Sanskrit as the Yogamālā and in Tibetan as Jorwé Trengwa, is a short verse manual of tantric meditative instruction compiled by the Indian paṇḍita Buddhakīrti from the oral instructions of various gurus, and translated into Tibetan by the novice Sherab Pal. Opening with homage to Vajrasattva, it presents a set of practices for the dawning of innate, stainless…

item.title: The Heart Vajra Words (Toh 1378)
item.description: The Heart Vajra Words, known in Sanskrit as the Hṛdayavajrapada and in Tibetan as Nyingpo Dorjé Tsik, is a very brief tantric instruction in verse, catalogued as Toh 1378 in the Tengyur, within its section of commentaries and treatises on the tantras. After paying homage to the glorious guru who reveals the all-pervading, undivided maṇḍala, it offers a few pith verses on completion-stage…

item.title: The Root Downfalls of the Vajrayāna Kālacakra (Toh 1379)
item.description: The Root Downfalls of the Vajrayāna Kālacakra, titled in Sanskrit Kālacakravajrayānamūlāpatti and in Tibetan Dorjé Tekpa Dükyi Khorlö Tsawé Tungwa, is a brief verse work on the vows of tantric practice according to the Kālacakra system. After paying homage to Kālacakra, Mañjuśrī and Vajrasattva, it sets out the fourteen root downfalls that a practitioner of the Vajra Vehicle must avoid, such as…

item.title: Summary Verses on the Glorious Kālacakra (Toh 1380)
item.description: The Summary Verses on the Glorious Kālacakra, known in Tibetan as Pal Dükyi Khorlo Domtsik, is a short verse digest composed by the great Indian paṇḍita Abhayākara and translated into Tibetan by the paṇḍita Jowo Ripa and the translator Kheu Gé Khorlo Drak. It condenses the whole scope of the Kālacakra system into a compact outline, dividing it into what is expressed and the words that express it…

item.title: The Lotus-Bearer: A Commentary on the Difficult Points of the Great King of Tantras, the Glorious Saṃvarodaya (Toh 1420)
item.description: The Padminī, or Lotus-Bearer, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Saṃvarodaya Mahātantrarājasya Padminī Nāma Pañcikā and in Tibetan as dPal sdom pa 'byung ba'i rgyud kyi rgyal po chen po'i dka' 'grel padma can, is a commentary on the difficult points of the Saṃvarodaya Tantra, one of the principal scriptures of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle of Buddhist yoginī tantra. item.title: The Sādhana of the Seven Syllables (Toh 1453)
item.description: The Sādhana of the Seven Syllables, in Sanskrit Saptākṣarasādhana and in Tibetan Yi ge bdun pa'i sgrub thabs, is a short tantric meditation manual devoted to Heruka, the wrathful form at the heart of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle, in union with his consort Vārāhī. It guides the practitioner through a full day of practice: rising at dawn, taking refuge and generating the mind of awakening, setting up a…

item.title: The Means of Accomplishment of Glorious Saṃvarodaya (Toh 1515)
item.description: The Means of Accomplishment of Glorious Saṃvarodaya, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Saṃvarodaya Sādhana and in Tibetan as Pal Dompa Jungwé Druptap, is a concise ritual manual for the meditative practice of the deity Cakrasaṃvara according to the Saṃvarodaya Tantra. After a verse of homage and a statement that it condenses the stages of practice taught in that tantra, it guides the practitioner…

item.title: The Means of Accomplishment of Vajravārāhī (Toh 1572)
item.description: The Means of Accomplishment of Vajravārāhī, known in Sanskrit as the Vajravārāhī Sādhana and in Tibetan as Dorjé Phakmö Drubthab, is a brief tantric practice text devoted to the goddess Vajravārāhī, the "Vajra Sow," a principal female deity of the Cakrasaṃvara cycle. It guides the practitioner through the visualization of the cosmos arising from seed syllables, the elemental maṇḍalas of wind…

item.title: The Commentary on the King of Tantras (Toh 1607)
item.description: The Commentary on the King of Tantras, the Glorious Catuṣpīṭha, called Smṛtinibandha, or The Cause of Recollection, known in Sanskrit as Śrīcatuṣpīṭhatantrarājasya Smṛtinibandha nāma Ṭīkā and in Tibetan as Gyü kyi Gyalpo Pal Den Shipé Drelpa Drenpé Gyutsen, is a detailed Indian commentary on the Catuṣpīṭha Tantra, a yoginī tantra whose name means "the Four Seats." item.title: An Explanation of the Noble Four Seats (Toh 1608)
item.description: An Explanation of the Noble Four Seats, known in Sanskrit as the Āryacatuṣpīṭhaṭīkā and in Tibetan as Phakpa Den Shyipai Nampar Shepa, is Toh 1608 in the Tengyur, where it belongs to the section of commentaries on the tantras. It is a commentary on the Catuṣpīṭha, the Four Seats Tantra, a yoginī tantra of the Unexcelled Yoga class, and its author describes it as an explanation that unties the…

item.title: The Means of Accomplishment of Mahāmāyā (Toh 1648)
item.description: The Means of Accomplishment of Mahāmāyā, in Sanskrit Mahāmāyāsādhana and in Tibetan Gyutrul Chenmö Druptap, is a short verse manual for the meditative practice of Mahāmāyā, a wrathful, four-faced and four-armed deity of the Mahāmāyā Tantra, one of the yoginī tantras of Highest Yoga Tantra. Opening with homage to Vajraḍākinī, it leads the practitioner through the preliminaries of purification…

item.title: The Extensive Commentary on the Glorious Buddhakapāla, Great King of Tantras, called Abhaya's Commentary on the Text (Toh 1654)
item.description: The Abhayapaddhati, in English "Abhaya's Commentary on the Text," known in full as the Extensive Commentary on the Glorious Buddhakapāla, Great King of Tantras (Sanskrit Śrībuddhakapālamahātantrarājaṭīkā Abhayapaddhati; Tibetan Pal Sangye Töpé Gyü kyi Gyalpo Chenpö Gyacher Drelpa Jikpa Mepé Zhungdrel), is a detailed Indian commentary on the Buddhakapāla Tantra, a yoginī tantra centered on the…

item.title: Śrīsarvabuddhasamāyogaḍākinīmāyāśaṃvaratantrārthodaraṭīkā (Toh 1659)
item.description: An Explanation of the Meaning of the Tantra of the Glorious Union with All Buddhas, the Ḍākinī Māyā Saṃvara, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Sarvabuddhasamāyoga Ḍākinījālasaṃvara Tantrārthodaraṭīkā and in Tibetan as Dpal sangs rgyas thams cad dang mnyam par sbyor ba mkha' 'gro sgyu ma bde mchog gi rgyud kyi don rnam par bshad pa, is an Indian commentary on the Sarvabuddhasamāyoga, an early tantra…

item.title: The Ornament of Union: A Commentary on the Union with All Buddhas, the Saṃvara of the Ḍākinī's Illusion (Toh 1660)
item.description: The Ornament of Union, known in Sanskrit as the Sarvabuddhasamāyogaḍākinīmāyāsaṃvaravṛtti Samāyogālaṃkāra and in Tibetan as Sangye Tamché Dang Nyampar Jorwa Khandroma Gyuma Dechok gi Drelpa Nyamjor gyi Gyen, is a commentary on the Union with All Buddhas, the Saṃvara of the Ḍākinī's Illusion, an early tantra of the great yoga class. item.title: Commentary on the Difficult Points of the Union with All Buddhas (Toh 1663)
item.description: The Commentary on the Difficult Points of the Union with All Buddhas, known in Sanskrit as the Sarvabuddhasamāyoga Pañjikā and in Tibetan as Sangyé Tamché Dang Nyampar Jorwé Kadrel, is a commentary on the Sarvabuddhasamāyoga Tantra, an early and influential yoginī tantra centered on Vajrasattva and on the union of all buddhas with the bliss of the ḍākinīs. item.title: The Rite of Recollecting Glorious Vajrasattva (Toh 1682)
item.description: The Rite of Recollecting Glorious Vajrasattva, known in Sanskrit as Śrī Vajrasattva Anusmṛti Nāma Vidhi and in Tibetan as Pal Dorjé Sempa Jesu Drenpé Choga, is a short tantric ritual manual devoted to the meditative recollection and worship of Vajrasattva, the embodiment of the purity of all the buddhas. item.title: Commentary on the Wrathful Chapter of the Tantra of Glorious Mahākāla, Called the Great Charnel Ground (Toh 1753)
item.description: The Commentary on the Wrathful Chapter of the Tantra of Glorious Mahākāla, Called the Great Charnel Ground, known in Sanskrit as the Śrī Mahākāla Tantra Rudra Kalpa Mahāśmaśāna Nāma Ṭīkā and in Tibetan as Dpal nag po chen po'i rgyud drag po'i brtag pa dur khrod chen po zhes bya ba'i 'grel pa, is Toh 1753 in the Tengyur, where it belongs to the section of commentaries on the tantras. item.title: The Clear Realization of Acala, Entitled Utter Delight (Toh 1783)
item.description: The Clear Realization of Acala, Entitled Utter Delight, known in Sanskrit as Acalābhisamaya Suratābhidhāna and in Tibetan as Mi gyowé ngönpar tokpa rabtu gawar ngönpar jöpa, is a tantric means of accomplishment (sādhana) devoted to Acala in his fierce form as Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa, the Great Wrathful One. item.title: An Extensive Commentary on the Eighteenth Chapter (Toh 1784a)
item.description: An Extensive Commentary on the Eighteenth Chapter, known in Sanskrit as the Aṣṭādaśapaṭalavistaravyākhyā and in Tibetan as Le'u bco brgyad pa'i rgya cher 'grel pa, is a tantric commentary devoted to the eighteenth chapter of the Guhyasamāja Tantra, the so-called later tantra that analyzes and clarifies the teachings of the seventeen chapters of the root tantra. item.title: An Extensive Commentary: The Lamp of All Secrets (Toh 1787)
item.description: The Lamp of All Secrets, an extensive commentary known in Sanskrit as the Sarvaguhyapradīpaṭīkā and in Tibetan as Gsang ba thams cad kyi sgron ma'i rgya cher 'grel pa, is Toh 1787 in the Tengyur, where it belongs among the commentaries on the tantras. It explains the Later Tantra, the eighteenth chapter of the Guhyasamāja Tantra, which gathers up and clarifies the meaning of the seventeen…

item.title: A Commentary Collecting the Difficult Points of the Illuminating Lamp (Toh 1792)
item.description: A Commentary Collecting the Difficult Points of the Illuminating Lamp, known in Sanskrit as the Pradīpoddyotana Viṣamapañjikā and in Tibetan as Drönma Selwar Jepé Kawa Tüpé Drelwa, is Toh 1792 in the Tengyur, where it belongs among the commentaries on the tantras.
